name: Triumph Bonneville 865 air-cooled DOHC parallel twin, 360-degree crank (Bonneville T100 / Thruxton, 2005-2015; main figures are the carburetted T100)
summary: Both pistons rise and fall together and the cylinders fire alternately one crank revolution apart, so the exhaust pulses are evenly spaced at 360 degrees: the classic smooth British-twin drone rather than the loping beat of the 270-degree versions. Each cylinder has its own header and silencer, joined by a balance pipe between the headers.

variant.value: carburetted Bonneville T100 865 (twin Keihin CVK 36); Thruxton and EFI figures given as *_thruxton / *_efi fields
variant.note: The cam timing, valve and limiter data are from the carburetted-model service manual. Carburettors were used through 2007, EFI from 2008 (UK) / 2009 (US) per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triumph_Bonneville ('Through 2007, all engines had carburettors'). No EFI-era service manual was opened, so cam data for EFI engines is not confirmed.

cylinders.note: Triumph factory service manual (carburetted models, 2006 scan), General Information p. 1.26, column '865 cc Bonneville T100'. 'Twin Cylinder 8 Valve DOHC'.

layout.note: Triumph factory service manual (carburetted models, 2006 scan), General Information p. 1.26, column '865 cc Bonneville T100'. 'Arrangement ... Transverse In-line'.

bore_mm.note: Triumph factory service manual (carburetted models, 2006 scan), General Information p. 1.26, column '865 cc Bonneville T100'. 'Bore x Stroke ... 90mm x 68mm'. Cylinder bore dia. on p. 1.27: 89.991 to 90.009 mm (std). Same 90 x 68 mm in the 2013 owner's handbook (https://www.triumphmotorcycles.co.uk/media-library/BC89FF86FC554E9A96862EBF62A748BC.pdf).

stroke_mm.note: Triumph factory service manual (carburetted models, 2006 scan), General Information p. 1.26, column '865 cc Bonneville T100'. 'Bore x Stroke ... 90mm x 68mm'.

rod_length_mm.note: Not in the service manual spec tables (pp. 1.26-1.27 list journal and small-end diameters only). A search snippet for an aftermarket rod (Spool Imports PSR5523, 'Bonneville Twin 2000 and up') showed 121.51 mm centre-to-centre, but the page (https://www.spoolimports.com/psr5523) returned errors and was never opened, so it is NOT recorded as a value.

compression_ratio.note: Triumph factory service manual (carburetted models, 2006 scan), General Information p. 1.26, column '865 cc Bonneville T100'. 'Compression Ratio ... 9.2 : 1' (same for Thruxton, p. 1.31). DISAGREEMENT: the 2013 owner's handbook for EFI models (https://www.triumphmotorcycles.co.uk/media-library/BC89FF86FC554E9A96862EBF62A748BC.pdf, p. 109/111) prints '10.2:1' for Bonneville, T100 and Thruxton and '9.2:1' only for the Scrambler. The carb-era owner's handbook on ManualsLib (https://www.manualslib.com/manual/538503/Triumph-Bonneville.html?page=93) gives 9.2:1. Unknown whether EFI engines really differ or the handbook is in error.

displacement_cc.note: Triumph factory service manual (carburetted models, 2006 scan), General Information p. 1.26, column '865 cc Bonneville T100'. 'Displacement ... 865cc'.

firing_order.note: Triumph factory service manual (carburetted models, 2006 scan), General Information p. 1.26, column '865 cc Bonneville T100'. Verbatim: 'Cylinder Numbering ... Left to Right', 'Firing Order ... 1-2', 'Firing Angle ... 360°'. So cylinder 1 is the left cylinder (rider's left), cylinder 2 the right. Same wording in the 2013 owner's handbook (https://www.triumphmotorcycles.co.uk/media-library/BC89FF86FC554E9A96862EBF62A748BC.pdf).

crank.value: 360-degree crank: both crank pins in line (0 degrees apart), pistons move together; balance shafts fitted
crank.note: Triumph factory service manual (carburetted models, 2006 scan), General Information p. 1.26, column '865 cc Bonneville T100'. Verbatim: 'Firing Angle ... 360°' for the Bonneville T100 (the Speedmaster column on the same page reads '270°'; p. 1.31 gives Thruxton '360°', Scrambler '270°'). Manual section 6 is titled 'Crankshaft/Rods/Balancers'. The manual states the firing angle, not the pin angle; pins-in-line is the standard meaning of a 360-degree twin, described at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Straight-twin_engine: 'In an engine with a 360 degree crankshaft, both pistons move up and down at the same time.' Also https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triumph_Bonneville_T100: '865 cc ... air-cooled, DOHC, parallel-twin, 360°'. NOTE: the 2013 owner's handbook (https://www.triumphmotorcycles.co.uk/media-library/BC89FF86FC554E9A96862EBF62A748BC.pdf, p. 109) prints '360° firing angle' for Bonneville/SE but '270° firing angle' in the T100 column, which contradicts the service manual, Triumph's own press specs (https://www.totalmotorcycle.com/motorcycles/2012models/2012-Triumph-Bonneville.htm: 'Air-cooled, DOHC, parallel-twin, 360º firing interval') and Wikipedia; treated as a handbook table error.

firing_intervals_deg.note: Triumph factory service manual (carburetted models, 2006 scan), General Information p. 1.26, column '865 cc Bonneville T100'. Verbatim: 'Firing Angle ... 360°' with 'Firing Order ... 1-2'. Even spacing: cyl 1 (left), 360 degrees later cyl 2 (right), 360 degrees later cyl 1. Corroborated by https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Straight-twin_engine: 'This set up results an even 360 degree firing interval'.

valves_per_cylinder.note: Triumph factory service manual (carburetted models, 2006 scan), General Information p. 1.26, column '865 cc Bonneville T100'. 'Twin Cylinder 8 Valve DOHC'. Bucket tappets ('Tappet Bucket Dia.').

intake_valve_dia_mm.note: Triumph factory service manual (carburetted models, 2006 scan), General Information p. 1.26, column '865 cc Bonneville T100'. 'Valve Head Dia. In. 31.0 mm'. Same for Thruxton (p. 1.31).

exhaust_valve_dia_mm.note: Triumph factory service manual (carburetted models, 2006 scan), General Information p. 1.26, column '865 cc Bonneville T100'. 'Valve Head Dia. Ex. 26.0 mm'.

intake_lift_mm.note: Triumph factory service manual (carburetted models, 2006 scan), General Information p. 1.26, column '865 cc Bonneville T100'. 'Valve Lift In. 9.5 mm'. Stated as valve lift (direct-acting buckets). Same for Thruxton.

exhaust_lift_mm.note: Triumph factory service manual (carburetted models, 2006 scan), General Information p. 1.26, column '865 cc Bonneville T100'. 'Valve Lift Ex. 9.4 mm'.

intake_duration_deg.note: Triumph factory service manual (carburetted models, 2006 scan), General Information p. 1.26, column '865 cc Bonneville T100'. 'Duration 232°', measured at 1.0 mm lift (4 + 180 + 48 = 232).

exhaust_duration_deg.note: Triumph factory service manual (carburetted models, 2006 scan), General Information p. 1.26, column '865 cc Bonneville T100'. 'Duration 220°', measured at 1.0 mm lift (33 + 180 + 7 = 220).

ivo_btdc.note: Triumph factory service manual (carburetted models, 2006 scan), General Information p. 1.26, column '865 cc Bonneville T100'. Verbatim: 'Valve Timing Inlet ... Open 4° BTDC (@ 1.0 mm Lift)'.

ivc_abdc.note: Triumph factory service manual (carburetted models, 2006 scan), General Information p. 1.26, column '865 cc Bonneville T100'. Verbatim: 'Close 48° ABDC (@ 1.0 mm Lift)'.

evo_bbdc.note: Triumph factory service manual (carburetted models, 2006 scan), General Information p. 1.26, column '865 cc Bonneville T100'. Verbatim: 'Exhaust Open 33° BBDC (@ 1.0 mm Lift)'.

evc_atdc.note: Triumph factory service manual (carburetted models, 2006 scan), General Information p. 1.26, column '865 cc Bonneville T100'. Verbatim: 'Close 7° ATDC (@ 1.0 mm Lift)'.

cam_timing_thruxton.note: Same manual p. 1.31, column 'Thruxton' (360°). Verbatim: 'Inlet ... Open 6° BTDC (@ 1.0 mm Lift) Close 50° ABDC (@ 1.0 mm Lift) Duration 235°; Exhaust Open 33° BBDC (@ 1.0 mm Lift) Close 8° ATDC (@ 1.0 mm Lift) Duration 221°'. Lift and valve sizes are the same as the T100 (9.5/9.4 mm, 31.0/26.0 mm). 6+180+50 = 236, so the printed 235 is off by one.

valve_clearance_mm.note: Triumph factory service manual (carburetted models, 2006 scan), General Information p. 1.26, column '865 cc Bonneville T100'. 'Valve Clearance In. 0.15 to 0.20 mm, Ex. 0.25 to 0.30 mm'.

redline_rpm.note: Same manual p. 1.28: 'Electronic Rev-Limiter ... 8000 rpm'. This is the ignition limiter, not a tachometer red-zone figure; the owner's handbook mentions a red zone without giving a number.

peak_power_kw.note: Triumph factory service manual (carburetted models, 2006 scan), General Information p. 1.26, column '865 cc Bonneville T100'. 'Max. Power (DIN 70020) ... 64PS @ 7250 RPM'; 64 PS x 0.7355 = 47.1 kW (converted). Carburetted T100.

peak_power_rpm.note: Triumph factory service manual (carburetted models, 2006 scan), General Information p. 1.26, column '865 cc Bonneville T100'. '64PS @ 7250 RPM'.

peak_torque_nm.note: Triumph factory service manual (carburetted models, 2006 scan), General Information p. 1.26, column '865 cc Bonneville T100'. 'Max. Torque ... 68Nm @ 6000 RPM'.

peak_torque_rpm.note: Triumph factory service manual (carburetted models, 2006 scan), General Information p. 1.26, column '865 cc Bonneville T100'. '68Nm @ 6000 RPM'.

peak_power_kw_thruxton.note: Same manual p. 1.31, carburetted Thruxton: 'Max. Power (DIN 70020) ... 70PS @ 7250 RPM' (70 x 0.7355 = 51.5 kW, converted); 'Max. Torque ... 72Nm @ 5750 RPM'.

peak_power_kw_efi.note: 2013 Triumph owner's handbook (publication 3851479 issue 1, EFI models), p. 109: Bonneville/SE and T100 'Maximum Power (95/1/EC) 68 PS @ 7,400 rpm' (68 x 0.7355 = 50.0 kW, converted); Thruxton '69 PS @ 7,400 rpm'. Triumph 2012 press specs at https://www.totalmotorcycle.com/motorcycles/2012models/2012-Triumph-Bonneville.htm give '68PS / 67bhp / 50 kW @ 7500rpm' (100 rpm different).

peak_torque_nm_efi.note: Same handbook p. 109: '68 Nm @ 5,800 rpm' (Thruxton '69 Nm @ 5,800 rpm').

intake_type.value: one carburettor per cylinder: twin Keihin CVK 36 constant-velocity carburettors (2005-2007); sequential electronic fuel injection with throttle bodies on 2008-on
intake_type.note: Service manual p. 1.29: 'Carburettors Type ... Keihin CVK 36', main jet 110, pilot jet 40, needle NBZT (T100). EFI: 2013 handbook (https://www.triumphmotorcycles.co.uk/media-library/BC89FF86FC554E9A96862EBF62A748BC.pdf) p. 113 'Sequential electronic fuel injection'.

throttle_dia_mm.note: No stated bore measurement found. The carburettor designation 'Keihin CVK 36' implies a nominal 36 mm bore, but that is an inference from the name, not a quoted dimension. EFI throttle body bore not found.

header_type.value: 2-into-2: one header pipe and one silencer per cylinder (one each side), with a balance pipe clamped between the two headers
header_type.note: Service manual p. 9.46, 'Header pipes - Bonneville, Bonneville T100 & Thruxton'. Verbatim: 'Slacken the clamp securing the header balance pipes together' and 'Fit both header pipes, joining the balance pipe whilst locating both headers correctly in the cylinder head ports'.

primary_dia_mm.note: Not in the manual. A vendor page (Norman Hyde, https://normanhyde.co.uk/?p=6144) says its 42 mm OD pipes fit 'earlier pre-injection Bonnevilles fitted with 38mm headers', which suggests 38 mm carb-era headers; parts-vendor statement, not recorded as a value.

exhaust_notes.value: Separate header and silencer each side, balance pipe between headers near the engine. T100: 'peashooter' silencers; base Bonneville 2009-on: upswept megaphones; Thruxton: reverse-cone megaphones. EFI models add catalysts and secondary air injection.
exhaust_notes.note: Balance pipe: service manual p. 9.46. Silencer styles: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triumph_Bonneville ('twin "peashooter" exhausts'; 'up-swept megaphone exhaust silencers'). Catalysts: 2013 handbook (https://www.triumphmotorcycles.co.uk/media-library/BC89FF86FC554E9A96862EBF62A748BC.pdf) p. 113 'Twin oxidation catalysts and pre-catalysts, with secondary air injection'. Silencer internal dimensions not found.

missing: rod_length_mm (only an unopened aftermarket listing suggests ~121.5 mm)
tachometer redline (only the 8000 rpm rev limiter was found)
cam timing and compression ratio confirmed for EFI (2008-on) engines

sources.what: Scan of the Triumph factory service manual for carburetted Bonneville, T100, America, Speedmaster, Thruxton and Scrambler (listed by the host as the 2006 service manual; 482 pages, RAR containing one PDF). Hosted on a third-party manuals mirror, but it is Triumph's own document. Pages read as images: 1.26-1.29 (865 cc T100/Speedmaster full specification), 1.31 (Scrambler/Thruxton), 9.46 (header pipes). Primary source for geometry, valves, cam timing, limiter, carburettors, balance pipe.

Triumph owner's handbook for Bonneville, Bonneville SE, T100, Thruxton, Scrambler (EFI models), publication 3851479 issue 1, copyright 06.2013, hosted on triumphmotorcycles.co.uk. Specifications pp. 109-113. Manufacturer document, but its T100 column prints a 270° firing angle and it gives 10.2:1 compression, both at odds with other sources.

Carburettor-era Triumph Bonneville owner's handbook on ManualsLib (104 pages), page 93: T100 865 cc, 64 PS @ 7,250 rpm, 68 Nm @ 6,000 rpm, 9.2:1, left to right, firing order 1-2. Read through a text extraction; used only as corroboration.
Total Motorcycle reprint of Triumph's 2012 Bonneville press specifications: '360º firing interval', 90 x 68 mm, 68PS/50 kW @ 7500 rpm, 68 Nm @ 5800 rpm.
Wikipedia, Triumph Bonneville T100: infobox lists the 865 cc engine as a 360° parallel twin, 90 x 68 mm.
Wikipedia, Triumph Bonneville: carburettor/EFI changeover years and silencer styles.
Wikipedia, Straight-twin engine: general description of 360-degree and 180-degree crank behaviour and firing intervals.
Web Cam aftermarket cam listing titled 'Triumph Bonneville 865 (T 100) (360°) DOHC 8v'. Performance grinds only, no stock data; used only as another '360°' label, no values taken.

vehicle.name: Triumph Bonneville T100, carburetted 865 cc (2005)
vehicle.chosen_because: The engine definition is the carburetted T100 865 cc (2005-2007); 2005 is the first year of the 865 cc T100.

curb_kg.quote: Dry weight [T100] 200 kg; Dry Fill 4.5 litres; Tank Capacity 16.6 Litres (?page=96)
curb_kg.note: Estimate, my calculation: 200 + 16.6 x 0.74 + 4.5 x 0.88 = about 216 kg. Carburettor-era owner's handbook on ManualsLib (covers 790 cc Bonneville/America and 865 cc T100/Thruxton/Speedmaster, no year printed; fits 2005-06). Read through a helper's text-extraction tool, not page images; ManualsLib refuses direct downloads. Conflicts: Triumph's 2005 press spec says 'Weight (Dry) 205kg (451lbs)' (https://www.totalmotorcycle.com/photos/2005models/2005models-Triumph-BonnevilleT100); the 2013 EFI T100 handbook says 'Wet Weight ... 230 kg' (https://www.triumphmotorcycles.co.uk/media-library/BC89FF86FC554E9A96862EBF62A748BC.pdf, p109).

gears.note: T100 column, printed p96. Cross-checked exactly against Triumph's own later EFI T100 handbook (https://www.triumphmotorcycles.co.uk/media-library/BC89FF86FC554E9A96862EBF62A748BC.pdf, PDF p114: '1st ... 2.73:1 (41/15)' ... '5th ... 1.07:1 (29/27)').

final_drive.quote: Primary Drive Ratio 1.74:1 (62/108); Final Drive Ratio 2.39:1 (18/43)
final_drive.note: T100 column (the 790 cc Bonneville has 17/43). My calculation: (108/62) x (43/18). Identical in the EFI handbook, PDF p114 ('1.74:1 (62/108)', '2.39:1 (18/43)').

tyre.note: Rider's 2005 T100 road test agrees: '130/80R-17 MEZ2 in the rear' (https://ridermagazine.com/2005-triumph-bonneville-t100-road-test/).

wheel_radius_m.note: My calculation, not published: unloaded geometric radius from the nominal size (rim diameter / 2 + section width x aspect ratio). The loaded rolling radius is a few percent smaller.

missing: top_speed_kmh: no Triumph figure and no period measured figure found. Looked in Rider's 2005 road test, Ultimate Motorcycling's 2005 review and Motorcyclist's 2005 review; MCN (HTTP 402) and bikesales (403) refused automated access. Wikipedia's '115 mph (est.)' and Motoplanete's 'environ 180 km/h' are estimates, not used.

sources.what: Triumph Bonneville / T100 / Thruxton / Speedmaster owner's handbook, carburettor era, on ManualsLib (pp.93-97): weights, capacities, gearing, tyres.
Triumph's own owner's handbook for the later fuel-injected Bonneville / T100 (2013 print): cross-check only; gearing identical.
Totalmotorcycle reprint of Triumph's 2005 T100 press specification: dry weight conflict (205 kg).
